title: Trace + Cost Field Lab: Standup & Investigation — 2026-05-21
body:
Attendees: Maya Patel (owner), Jon Li, Priya Rao, Ethan Brooks, Lina Gomez, (notes taken live)

TL;DR
- Brief spike in trace ingestion and downstream query cost observed starting 2026-05-19 03:00 UTC; billable telemetry for traces increased ~42% week-over-week for the same request volume.
- Suspect: unintended change to SDK default sampling and a new debug span emitted by the search-service 2026-05-18 patch.
- Short-term mitigation: revert search-service change and lower sampling proportion for low-priority routes. Mid-term: add automated sampling governance + dashboard alerts.

Summary of what we saw
- Metrics: trace_ingested_count (daily): baseline ~1.4M -> peaked 2.1M on 2026-05-19.
- Costs: observed RUM/trace BigQuery export cost jump and increased egress to tracing-backend; estimated incremental cost ~$3.2k/week.
- Affected dashboards: trace-overview, latency-by-route, span-distribution. Several panels showed heavier tail of spans per trace for search-service (median spans 12 -> 48).
- Time window: spike coincides with deployment window 2026-05-18 21:40 UTC (search-service v2.11.4).

Investigation steps & findings (what we ran)
1) Cross-check releases: reviewed GH PR 1289 (search-service): added DEBUG logging + newSpan("db.query-explain") for every SQL call (unbounded).
2) Query traces per service (PromQL + bigquery):
   - prom: sum(rate(traces_received_total{service="search-service"}[1h])) by (service) -> 3.6x bump 2026-05-19 03:00
   - bq: SELECT service, COUNT(1) as spans FROM `telemetry.traces` WHERE DATE(timestamp) BETWEEN '2026-05-18' AND '2026-05-20' GROUP BY service ORDER BY spans DESC
3) Span composition: many small debug spans with tag debug=true; made CSV export for the top 10 trace IDs showing repeated db.explain spans.
4) Sampling config audit: frontends (edge) sampling remained at 0.03 (3%) but internal middleware (search-service) introduced high-volume internal traces ignoring parent sampling.
5) Dashboard query cost: several panels used unbounded BigQuery scans (no expiration filter), contributing to BigQuery slot/scan increases.

Conclusions so far
- Primary root cause: application-level change emitted excessive debug spans and bypassed standard sampling controls.
- Secondary contributor: dashboard queries lacking date filters and a slow alert that should have detected ingestion slope earlier.

Immediate mitigations (today)
- Rollback: Priya to open rollback PR for search-service v2.11.4 (OBS-427). Target: 2026-05-22 02:00 UTC.
- Sampling override: Jon to deploy a temporary sampling middleware on search-service that forces sample_rate<=0.02 for internal spans. Target: 2026-05-21 23:00 UTC.
- Dashboard fix: Lina to modify heavy-cost panels to add default +30d date filter and query cost estimate comments. Target: 2026-05-22.

Short-term follow-ups (this sprint)
- Add guardrails: create lightweight linter rule for PRs that add new spans or logging (search for "newSpan") — owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-05-28.
- Alerting: create a steep-slope alert on traces_received_total (10% sustained for 1h) with paging. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-05-24.
- Cost dashboard: add panel with weekly delta and 7d projection for trace-related BigQuery scan bytes. Owner: Lina. ETA: 2026-05-26.

Longer-term changes (next quarter)
- Sampling governance: centralized sampling policy (config + SDK hooks) and enforced via build pipeline.
- Auto-prune: investigate adding an ingestion-time filter to drop spans with tag debug=true unless explicitly enabled.
- Dashboard reviewer workflow: require query cost sign-off for any dashboard panel that references raw telemetry tables.

Open questions / unknowns
- Why did the search-service PR add unguarded debug spans? (Priya to follow up with service owner in infra-review thread).
- Are there other services that bypass sampling? (Jon to run service-scan for newSpan usage across repos).
- How much of the BigQuery cost is attributable to exports vs ad-hoc dashboard queries? Need billing split (Finance tagging).

Notes to self (informal)
- Reminder: add a small section to the README about "preferred span cardinality" with examples.
- Keep export window small for heavy tables; maybe move raw trace export to hourly partition with TTL 30d.

Meeting artifacts / reproducible queries (copy of what we ran)
- PromQL used: sum(rate(traces_received_total{service=~".*"}[5m])) by (service)
- BigQuery sample for high-span traces:
  SELECT trace_id, service, COUNT(1) as span_count
  FROM `telemetry.traces`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY trace_id, service
  HAVING span_count > 30
  ORDER BY span_count DESC

Action items (explicit)
- Priya Rao: rollback search-service v2.11.4 (create PR, coordinate deploy) — due 2026-05-22 02:00 UTC.
- Jon Li: sampling override middleware + scan repos for newSpan usage — due 2026-05-24.
- Lina Gomez: dashboard cost fixes + new cost panel — due 2026-05-22 (quick fixes) and 2026-05-26 (panel).
- Ethan Brooks: create slope alert, add escalation policy to PagerDuty playbook — due 2026-05-24.
- Maya Patel: linter rule design doc + add README span cardinality section — due 2026-05-28.

Next sync
- Quick check-in tomorrow 2026-05-22 09:30 PT (15m). Full postmortem draft by 2026-05-27.

Misc
- Link to PR for rollback (TBD) will be added to linked_artifacts.
- Slack thread: #obs-team (thread pinned) — contains traces screenshots and CSV export.

Status: starting mitigations now; aim to return to baseline traces ingestion within 24–36 hours after rollback + sampling override.
